flow.costPlain: What Nu pays to fund its lending and move money — interest to depositors and lenders, payment-processing costs, and money set aside for loans that may not be repaid.
flow.grossPlain: What's left after paying the direct cost of providing financial services — funding, transactions and credit losses.

opex.name: Customer support and operations
opex.note: Running the app, support and back office for 143 million customers — just 3.8% of revenue. Up 28%, slower than revenue growth.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Offices, people, legal and finance — the biggest running cost, 10.2% of revenue. Up 69%, the fastest-growing opex line in dollars (+$241M).

opex.name: Marketing
opex.note: Ads and customer acquisition — only 2.2% of revenue, because most growth is word of mouth. Up 79% off a small base.

follow100Note: Nu keeps about $18.75 of every $100 of revenue. Credit losses ($28.67) now cost more per $100 than funding ($27.00). Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Headlines quote managerial revenue $6,258.5M and gross profit $2,597.6M, but this Sankey uses the IFRS accounting P&L; net income $1,091.6M is identical under both.
oneTimers: No discrete one-time charge is quantified in this release. Excluding non-recurring items, risk-adjusted NIM rose to 12.7% from 11.9% in Q2 (vs 12.1% reported) — implying some non-recurring drag on margins — but the release does not size the items, so no ex-charge figures can be given.

Some expenses shifted into Q4: management says the improved full-year efficiency guidance (19–19.5%) reflects year-to-date performance “and a sequential increase in the fourth quarter” — Q3's cost lines are flattered slightly by timing.

Share-based compensation ($216.1M) and share repurchases ($500.4M) are nine-month figures from the statement of changes in equity, not Q3 alone — noted here so they aren't mistaken for quarterly numbers.
otherDetail: Other income added $21.8M (small gains outside the core business), less Nu's $8.3M share of losses from minority investments.
pngFooterNote: Sankey uses the IFRS P&L; headlines quote the managerial measure.

segments.name: Interest income & instrument gains
segments.note: What Nu earns lending money and on its financial instruments — 86% of revenue. Up 40% as the credit portfolio grew 33% and rates stayed high.

segments.name: Fee and commission income
segments.note: Card interchange, account and service fees — 14% of revenue, up 37%. The smaller, faster-growing slice.

takeaways.text: Net income hit a record $1.09B with a 32% ROE, and the efficiency ratio improved to a best-ever 19.3% — the bank spends less than 20 cents to make a dollar of gross profit, an almost unheard-of ratio in banking. That operating leverage is the whole investment case.
takeaways.title: Record profit, built on cheap operations

takeaways.text: Expected credit losses jumped 71% year over year — far faster than the 33% loan-book growth — and the 90+ day delinquency rate rose to 7.3% from 6.9% last quarter and 6.7% a year ago. Management says risk-adjusted NIM actually improved excluding non-recurring items (12.7% vs 11.9% in Q2), but the direction of delinquencies is the quarter's one clear negative.
takeaways.title: Credit quality is the thing to watch

takeaways.text: Mexico added 870,000 customers in its first quarter as a licensed bank; Colombia is now the country's largest credit-card issuer by cardholders; and Nu US launched September 10 (customers in all 50 states within weeks) with Nu Global live in 37 countries. Brazil is nearly saturated — 65% of adults already bank with Nu — so future growth has to come from these new fronts.
takeaways.title: The story is now bigger than Latin America

verdict: Nu posted a record $1.09 billion profit as revenue grew 37% on an FX-neutral basis and the efficiency ratio hit a best-ever 19.3%, but credit is the price of that growth — expected credit losses jumped 71% and the 90+ day delinquency rate rose to 7.3% — even as the bank added 3.7 million customers and took its first steps beyond Latin America with launches in the U.S.
